newsitem.title: INDIA: India's VSNL to broadbase issue bankers.
newsitem.headline: India's VSNL to broadbase issue bankers.

text.p: India's state-run overseas telecommunication monopoly, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited (VSNL), has decided to broadbase the syndicate of managers for its Euro issue of shares, the Economic Times said on Monday.

The newspaper said VSNL planned to add six to eight co-managers for the global depositary receipt (GDR) issue to an existing three by January 9, the deadline for selection of co-managers. The issue is expected in February, it said.
VSNL will retain investment banks Kleinwort Benson, Salomon Brothers and Jardine Fleming, who were appointed in 1994 for an aborted issue, as lead managers to the upcoming offer, it said.
The newspaper said VSNL will float 15 million GDRs in overseas markets and sell four to five million shares in the domestic market. A GDR is a warrant exchangeable for two shares.
It quoted finance ministry sources as saying that the number of co-managers will be decided on the day of the selection.
"The number of co-managers to be added will be six or more, but not more than eight," it said.
Market sources estimate the issue size will be somewhere between $650 million and $800 million.
VSNL has a monopoly over overseas telephone calls, data transmission and Internet services.
